name: instance variables declared with explicit `private` vs declared with no access modifier (default/package-private)
side_a: No_deduct when both required instance variables carry an explicit `private` access modifier at class level (e.g. `private double capacity;`), regardless of naming, extra locals, or `this.` usage.
side_b: Deduct when a required instance variable is declared at class level with no access modifier (or a non-private one), e.g. `double capacity;` — the rubric requires the variables be *private*, so default/package-private visibility fails this point even though the fields otherwise exist and are of the right type.

name: Sub-item scope: header signature only vs. body/return-value correctness also counted
side_a: Do not deduct as long as the declared header is `public double updateAmount(double <param>)`. Errors in the method body — returning the wrong value, omitting or mis-writing the refill check — belong to other sub-items and must not cost this signature point.
side_b: Deduct if the method does not actually behave as specified (e.g., returns `capacity` instead of the remaining amount, or returns the pre-refill amount), treating a wrong return *value* as failing the 'returns double' requirement.

name: Instance-variable visibility: irrelevant to the method-header bullet vs. non-private fields taint the 'public' check
side_a: Do not deduct for how the instance variables are declared (missing `private`, package-private, or different names); only the `updateAmount` declaration is evaluated here.
side_b: Deduct if the class's instance variables are not declared `private`, treating sloppy access modifiers anywhere in the class as a violation of the modifier requirement.

name: Returns the object's updated amount (post-refill) vs returns some other value (pre-refill snapshot or capacity)
side_a: no_deduct: on every path the method returns the instance field holding the current amount as it stands after the subtraction and any refill (e.g. `return amount;` / `return this.currentAmount;` as the single exit after the if-block).
side_b: deduct: at least one return path yields a value other than the final stored amount — e.g. unconditionally `return capacity;`, or returning a saved pre-refill value (`return amountBeforeRefillCheck;`) when a refill occurred.

name: Strict `< 0.25*capacity` refill test vs inclusive `<= 0.25*capacity`
side_a: no_deduct: the refill condition triggers only when the remaining amount is strictly below one quarter of capacity (`if (amount < 0.25 * capacity)`).
side_b: deduct: the refill condition also fires when the amount equals exactly one quarter of capacity (`if (amount <= 0.25 * capacity)`), an off-by-one boundary error.

name: Any state-derived amount returned from updateAmount counts vs. the returned value must be exactly the post-update remaining amount
side_a: No deduct: award the point whenever updateAmount ends in a `return` of a value drawn from the bottle's tracked state (the amount field, the capacity field, or a snapshot of the amount taken during the method), even if it is the wrong quantity or a stale/pre-refill value — choosing the wrong quantity is a logic error scored under a different rubric point, not under 'returns the remaining amount'.
side_b: Deduct: award the point only if the value actually returned is the correctly updated remaining amount on every execution path, so returning the capacity field or a pre-refill snapshot loses the point.
